chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Fadalah ibn Ayyub narrated to us from Sa'dan al-Wasiti, from 'Ajlan Abi Salih, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

O Aba Salih, when you carry a funeral bier, imagine that it is you who is being carried, or that you are asking your Lord to return you to the world so that you may do [good], and see what you will resume [doing].

Then he said: 'How astounding it is for a community whose former members have been confined away [in their graves] from their latter ones [who are alive], then a caller calls out among them for departure [from this world] while they are [busy] playing!'

key_terms.أَوَّلُهُمْ عَلَى آخِرِهِمْ: The former ones upon the latter ones (referring to those who died before the living)

ai.seo_question: How should one contemplate death when attending a funeral according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) employs the rhetorical device of *takhayyul* (visualization) to transform the passive act of witnessing a funeral into an active spiritual audit, urging the believer to imagine returning to the world to rectify their deeds. This narration, found in *Kitab al-Zuhd*, underscores the Shia emphasis on *mawt* (death) as a catalyst for *muhasaba* (self-accounting), contrasting the negligence of the living with the finality of the dead. The Imam’s concluding remark on those 'playing' while their predecessors are called away highlights the urgency of seizing the present moment before the call of the Angel of Death arrives.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 1.Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated to us [saying], “Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb narrated to us from Saʿdān al-Wāsiṭī, from ʿAjlān Abī Ṣāliḥ who said, ‘Abū ʿAbdillāh said [to me], “O Abā Ṣāliḥ, when a [funeral] bier is lifted, imagine that it is you who is being carried [upon it], or that you are the one asking your Lord to return you to the world so that you may do good deeds, and see then what you will resume [of your actions].”

Then he said, “How astounding it is for a community whose former members have been confined away [in their graves] from their latter ones [who are alive], then a caller calls out among them for departure [from this world] while they are [busy] playing!”’”
